2. **A fake environ is built** [`src/flask/app.py:1470-1477`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1470-L1477) `test_request_context` uses Flask's `EnvironBuilder`, which fills the base URL from `SERVER_NAME` (or `localhost`), `APPLICATION_ROOT` and `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME` [`src/flask/testing.py:65-83`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/testing.py#L65-L83).
3. **Entering the with-block pushes** [`src/flask/ctx.py:433-435`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L433-L435) `RequestContext.__enter__` is just `push()`, and `__exit__` is `pop(exc_value)`.
4. **An app context is pushed if needed** [`src/flask/ctx.py:370-376`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L370-L376) If an app context for the same app is already active it is reused, and `None` is stored so this request context will not pop it later.
5. **The app context gets a fresh g** [`src/flask/ctx.py:245-254`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L245-L254) `AppContext.__init__` creates a URL adapter without a request (only possible when `SERVER_NAME` is set) and a new `g`. `push` sets the ContextVar, keeps the token and sends `appcontext_pushed`.
6. **Reading request.args resolves the proxy** [`src/flask/globals.py:42-48`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/globals.py#L42-L48) `request.args` becomes `_cv_request.get().request.args`. With nothing pushed, the proxy raises `RuntimeError` with the 'Working outside of request context' text [`src/flask/globals.py:35-41`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/globals.py#L35-L41).
7. **Pop runs teardown only for the last push** [`src/flask/ctx.py:396-414`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L396-L414) A context can be pushed more than once (for example by `stream_with_context`). Only when the last token is popped are `teardown_request` functions run and the request closed.
8. **Tokens are reset and the app context is popped** [`src/flask/ctx.py:415-431`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L415-L431) The ContextVar goes back to its previous value, the environ's back-reference to the request is cleared to avoid a reference cycle, and the app context pushed in step 4 is popped. Popping the wrong context raises `AssertionError`.
9. **The app context tears down** [`src/flask/ctx.py:256-272`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L256-L272) On its last pop the app context runs `teardown_appcontext` functions (the tutorial closes its database here), resets `_cv_app` and sends `appcontext_popped`.
10. **Ways to keep a context alive longer** [`src/flask/helpers.py:108-135`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py#L108-L135) `stream_with_context` re-pushes the current request context inside a generator so streamed responses can still read `request`. `copy_current_request_context` does the same for greenlets [`src/flask/ctx.py:187-193`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L187-L193), and the test client can keep contexts after a request with `with client:` [`src/flask/testing.py:185-191`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/testing.py#L185-L191).

> **Checkpoint:** Inside `with app.app_context():` a test calls `client.get('/')`, and the view sets `g.x = 1`. After the call, can the test read `g.x`?
> - No, every request gets a fresh g
> - Yes; the request reused the active app context, so it shares that g
> - Only if the view returns g
> - It raises AssertionError
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Yes; the request reused the active app context, so it shares that g. `RequestContext.push` reuses an active app context for the same app instead of creating one [`src/flask/ctx.py:370-376`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L370-L376), so `g` is the one from your with-block.</details>

### Registering a blueprint

*standard · 7 min*

**In short:** A blueprint records your decorators as deferred functions and replays them when registered, prefixing rules with `url_prefix` and endpoints with the blueprint's dotted name.

Think of a blueprint as a recorder for setup calls. While you decorate, nothing touches an app: `Blueprint.add_url_rule` validates names and records `lambda s: s.add_url_rule(...)` [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:412-441`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L412-L441). Hook decorators fill the blueprint's own registries, exactly as on an app, because both inherit from `Scaffold`.

`app.register_blueprint(bp, **options)` plays the recording [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:273-377`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L273-L377):
1. Compute the registered name, `options.get("name", bp.name)`, prefixed by the parent's name when nested; refuse a name already in `app.blueprints`.
2. Store the blueprint, mark it registered (its setup methods now raise) and build a `BlueprintSetupState` that resolves `url_prefix`, `subdomain` and `url_defaults` from the options or the blueprint's own values [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:41-85`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L41-L85).
3. Add the blueprint's static route if it has a `static_folder`.
4. Merge the blueprint's hook dicts into the app, renaming the `None` key to the blueprint's name [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:379-410`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L379-L410).
5. Call each recorded function with the state. For routes that is `BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule`, which joins the prefix, prefixes the endpoint and calls `app.add_url_rule` [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:87-116`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L87-L116).
6. Attach the blueprint's CLI group and register nested blueprints with combined prefixes and subdomains.

Registering the same blueprint twice works with a different `name=`; hooks are merged again only for a new name [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:330-332`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L330-L332). The `app_*` decorators (`before_app_request`, `app_errorhandler`, `app_template_filter`) use `record_once`, so they reach the app's global scope once however often the blueprint is registered [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:232-244`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L232-L244).

After registration a blueprint is just names: at request time Flask only sees dotted endpoints and scoped registries.

**Flow: Registering a blueprint: recorded decorators replayed onto the app** (trigger: The tutorial's create_app() calls app.register_blueprint(auth.bp))

1. **The blueprint is created at import time** [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/auth.py:16`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/auth.py#L16) The constructor rejects empty names and names with a dot, then sets up `deferred_functions` and the list of nested blueprints [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:195-211`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L195-L211).
2. **@bp.route records instead of registering** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:412-441`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L412-L441) `Scaffold.route` calls `add_url_rule`, which on a blueprint checks for dots and then stores `lambda s: s.add_url_rule(...)` for later.
3. **@bp.before_app_request records an app-wide hook** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:553-561`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L553-L561) The `app_` variants use `record_once` and write to the app's `None` scope, so `load_logged_in_user` runs before every request, not just `/auth/*`.
4. **The app hands off to the blueprint** [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:569-595`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L569-L595) `register_blueprint` is a setup method, so it fails after the first request. Options such as `url_prefix=` and `name=` override the blueprint's own values.
5. **The registered name must be unique** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:302-314`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L302-L314) The name is `name_prefix.name` (the prefix is set for nested blueprints). Registering a second blueprint under a taken name raises `ValueError` and suggests `name=`.
6. **A setup state is created** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:316-321`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L316-L321) The blueprint is stored in `app.blueprints` and marked registered (so its own setup methods now fail). `BlueprintSetupState` resolves the `url_prefix`, `subdomain` and URL defaults for this registration [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:64-85`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L64-L85).
7. **Hook dicts are merged under the blueprint's name** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:379-410`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L379-L410) The blueprint's own `None`-scoped hooks are copied into the app under the key `auth`, error handlers too, so at request time they apply only when `request.blueprints` contains `auth`.
8. **Deferred functions are replayed** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:334-335`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L334-L335) Each stored lambda is called with the state.
9. **Rules get the prefix, endpoints get the name** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:87-116`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L87-L116) `/login` becomes `/auth/login`, endpoint `login` becomes `auth.login`, and the call ends in the app's normal `add_url_rule`, which adds the Rule to `url_map` and the function to `view_functions`.
10. **CLI commands and nested blueprints** [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:337-377`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L337-L377) Blueprint CLI commands are added to `app.cli` as a group named after the blueprint (or merged in when `cli_group=None`). Nested blueprints are registered recursively with combined prefixes, subdomains and a `name_prefix` of the parent's name.
11. **At request time the dotted endpoint picks the scopes** [`src/flask/wrappers.py:161-195`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/wrappers.py#L161-L195) `request.blueprint` is everything before the last dot of the endpoint, and `request.blueprints` lists it and its parents, which is how hooks and error handlers for the right blueprints are found [`src/flask/helpers.py:627-634`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py#L627-L634).

> **Checkpoint:** `bp = Blueprint('api', __name__, url_prefix='/api')` has `@bp.route('/users')` and is registered with `app.register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix='/v2')`. What URL and endpoint result?
> - /api/users and api.users
> - /v2/users and api.users
> - /v2/api/users and v2.users
> - /users and users
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>/v2/users and api.users. Options passed at registration override the blueprint's own prefix [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:72-77`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L72-L77), and the endpoint is the registered name plus the function's endpoint [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py:112`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py#L112).</details>

### Sessions: opened at push, saved in process_response

*standard · 7 min*

**In short:** The default session is loaded from a signed cookie when the request context is pushed, and written back in `process_response` only if it changed or must be refreshed.

Two calls into the request lifecycle carry the whole feature: `open_session` during `RequestContext.push` [`src/flask/ctx.py:384-389`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L384-L389) and `save_session` at the end of `process_response` [`src/flask/app.py:1321-1322`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1321-L1322). Everything else is in `sessions.py`.

**Opening.** Without a `SECRET_KEY`, `get_signing_serializer` returns `None`, `open_session` returns `None`, and the context installs a `NullSession`, which raises a 'no secret key was set' error on any write [`src/flask/sessions.py:97-111`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L97-L111). With a key, the cookie named by `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` (default `session`) is loaded with `max_age` set to `PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME` (31 days); a bad or expired signature quietly gives an empty session [`src/flask/sessions.py:337-349`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L337-L349).

**Tracking.** The session is a Werkzeug `CallbackDict`: writes set `modified` and `accessed`; `__getitem__`, `get` and `setdefault` set `accessed` [`src/flask/sessions.py:74-94`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L74-L94). Mutating a nested value does not count.

**Saving.** If the session was accessed, `Vary: Cookie` is added. If it is now empty and was modified, the cookie is deleted. If it is unchanged it is skipped, unless it is permanent and `SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST` is on. Otherwise it is serialized, signed and set with `HttpOnly` by default, plus `Secure`, `SameSite`, `Partitioned`, `Domain` and `Path` from config [`src/flask/sessions.py:351-399`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L351-L399). Only `session.permanent = True` gives the cookie an expiry date; otherwise it lasts until the browser closes [`src/flask/sessions.py:237-245`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L237-L245).

**Rotating keys.** Put old keys in `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`. They are accepted when reading, while new cookies are signed with `SECRET_KEY`, which is placed last in the key list as ItsDangerous expects [`src/flask/sessions.py:321-326`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L321-L326). `test_session_secret_key_fallbacks` walks through a full rotation [`tests/test_basic.py:374-399`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/tests/test_basic.py#L374-L399).

To store sessions elsewhere, implement `open_session` and `save_session` on a `SessionInterface` subclass and assign it to `app.session_interface` [`src/flask/sessions.py:114-149`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L114-L149).

**Flow: Logging in: writing the session cookie and reading it back** (trigger: A user submits the tutorial's login form; the next page load knows who they are)

1. **Pushing the context opens the session** [`src/flask/ctx.py:384-389`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L384-L389) Only the first push opens it, so `stream_with_context` does not reload the session.
2. **A signing serializer is built from the keys** [`src/flask/sessions.py:317-335`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L317-L335) No `SECRET_KEY` means no serializer, which leads to a `NullSession`. Otherwise the keys are `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` followed by the current key, with salt `cookie-session`, HMAC key derivation and SHA-1 [`src/flask/sessions.py:303-315`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L303-L315).
3. **The cookie is verified and decoded** [`src/flask/sessions.py:337-349`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L337-L349) No cookie gives an empty session. A cookie older than `PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME` (31 days by default) or with a bad signature is silently replaced by an empty session.
4. **The view writes to the session** [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/auth.py:101-105`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/auth.py#L101-L105) `login` clears the session and stores the user id, then redirects.
5. **The session dict notices the change** [`src/flask/sessions.py:74-94`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L74-L94) `SecureCookieSession` is a Werkzeug `CallbackDict`: any write sets `modified` and `accessed`, and reads set `accessed`. Changes inside a nested list or dict are not seen.
6. **flash() writes through the session too** [`src/flask/helpers.py:326-335`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py#L326-L335) It reads the list, appends, and assigns it back, so the change is detected even by session backends that store data elsewhere.
7. **process_response asks the interface to save** [`src/flask/app.py:1321-1322`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1321-L1322) This happens after all `after_request` functions, so they can still change the session.
8. **Empty or unchanged sessions are skipped** [`src/flask/sessions.py:362-384`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L362-L384) If the session was read at all, `Vary: Cookie` is added so caches do not mix users. An emptied session deletes the cookie. Otherwise the cookie is written only if `modified`, or if the session is permanent and `SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST` is true [`src/flask/sessions.py:247-261`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L247-L261).
9. **The cookie is serialized, signed and set** [`src/flask/sessions.py:386-398`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L386-L398) Values are tagged so tuples, bytes, datetimes and UUIDs survive JSON [`src/flask/json/tag.py:289-295`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L289-L295). Only permanent sessions get an `Expires` date [`src/flask/sessions.py:237-245`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L237-L245); cookie flags come from the `SESSION_COOKIE_*` config.
10. **The next request loads the user** [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/auth.py:32-43`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/auth.py#L32-L43) A `before_app_request` hook reads the id from the freshly opened session and stores the user row on `g.user` for this request.

> **Checkpoint:** A view runs `session['cart'].append(item)` and the item is gone on the next request. Why?
> - The cookie is too large
> - No write to the session dict happened, so `modified` stayed False and the cookie was not rewritten
> - Lists cannot be stored in sessions
> - SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is off
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>No write to the session dict happened, so `modified` stayed False and the cookie was not rewritten. Only the top-level dict is tracked; nested changes need `session.modified = True` [`src/flask/sessions.py:61-66`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L61-L66).</details>

### The `flask` command: finding the app and running commands

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** The `flask` command is a Click group whose options configure the environment, whose `ScriptInfo` finds and caches your app, and whose app commands always run inside an app context.

Read the CLI as three questions.

**How does it know which app?** `--app`, or `FLASK_APP` through Click's `auto_envvar_prefix="FLASK"`, is stored on `ScriptInfo` [`src/flask/cli.py:440-446`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L440-L446). `ScriptInfo.load_app` then tries, in order: an explicit `create_app` callback (used by custom `FlaskGroup`s and the test runner), the import path, or `wsgi.py` and `app.py` in the current directory [`src/flask/cli.py:333-364`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L333-L364). The import path is a file path or dotted module, optionally followed by `:name` or `:factory(args)`; the arguments are parsed as Python literals with `ast`, never evaluated as code [`src/flask/cli.py:120-165`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L120-L165). The result is cached in `_loaded_app`.

**Why does `current_app` work in my command?** `FlaskGroup.get_command` pushes an app context for the loaded app before returning one of its commands [`src/flask/cli.py:628-634`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L628-L634), and `AppGroup.command` wraps commands in `with_appcontext` anyway [`src/flask/cli.py:413-427`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L413-L427). Built-in commands that need the app (`shell`, `routes`) use `@with_appcontext` explicitly.

**Where do environment settings come from?** `--env-file` is processed first and loads `.flaskenv`, then `.env`, then the given file, without overriding variables already set in the environment [`src/flask/cli.py:698-763`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L698-L763). `--debug` writes `FLASK_DEBUG` before the app is imported, so a factory can read it. Commands from installed packages are discovered through the `flask.commands` entry point group [`src/flask/cli.py:600-607`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L600-L607).

`flask routes` is a short, readable example of a command that uses the app: it lists `url_map.iter_rules()`, hides HEAD and OPTIONS unless `--all-methods` is given, and sorts by endpoint, methods, rule or match order [`src/flask/cli.py:1048-1107`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L1048-L1107).

**Flow: `flask --app flaskr run --debug`: from the shell to a running server** (trigger: A developer types flask --app flaskr run --debug in a terminal)

1. **The console script calls cli.main()** [`src/flask/cli.py:1110-1123`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L1110-L1123) `pyproject.toml` maps the `flask` executable to `flask.cli:main` [`pyproject.toml:82-83`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/pyproject.toml#L82-L83); `python -m flask` does the same through `__main__.py`.
2. **make_context prepares the run** [`src/flask/cli.py:657-676`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L657-L676) It sets `FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI=true` (so `app.run()` in your module becomes a no-op) and creates the `ScriptInfo` that every command receives.
3. **The group's options are processed first** [`src/flask/cli.py:572-577`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L572-L577) The eager `--env-file` and `--app` go first: `--env-file` loads `.flaskenv`, `.env` and the given file [`src/flask/cli.py:493-512`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L493-L512), `--app` stores the import path on `ScriptInfo`, and `--debug` writes `FLASK_DEBUG=1` into the environment so even a factory can see it [`src/flask/cli.py:479-481`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L479-L481).
4. **The command is looked up** [`src/flask/cli.py:609-634`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L609-L634) Built-in commands (`run`, `shell`, `routes`) and plugin commands from the `flask.commands` entry point are found without importing your app. Only app commands such as `init-db` require loading the app, after which an app context is pushed for them.
5. **run_command loads the app** [`src/flask/cli.py:954-971`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L954-L971) In the reloader's child process a load error is printed and re-raised on every request, so the browser debugger can show it instead of the server dying.
6. **The import path is resolved** [`src/flask/cli.py:333-364`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L333-L364) `module:name` is split on the first colon not followed by a slash (so Windows paths work). `prepare_import` walks up past folders containing `__init__.py`, puts the parent on `sys.path` and returns the dotted module name [`src/flask/cli.py:200-226`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L200-L226).
7. **The app or factory is found** [`src/flask/cli.py:41-91`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L41-L91) Without a name, Flask looks for `app` or `application`, then a single `Flask` instance in the module, then a `create_app` or `make_app` factory callable with no arguments. `flaskr` is found through its `create_app` [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py:6-8`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py#L6-L8).
8. **Debug is applied through the property** [`src/flask/cli.py:366-372`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L366-L372) Assigning `app.debug` updates `config['DEBUG']` and, unless `TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD` is set, Jinja's `auto_reload` [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:562-567`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L562-L567).
9. **Werkzeug's development server starts** [`src/flask/cli.py:973-993`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L973-L993) The reloader and debugger default to the debug flag, threads are on by default, and the banner prints the app path and debug state. From here every request runs the request flow.

> **Checkpoint:** `flask --app 'myapp:create_app(os.environ["X"])' run` fails to load. Why?
> - Factories cannot take arguments
> - Factory arguments must be Python literals; `ast.literal_eval` rejects expressions
> - The quotes are wrong for Windows
> - The factory must be named make_app
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Factory arguments must be Python literals; `ast.literal_eval` rejects expressions. Arguments are parsed with `ast.literal_eval`, and anything else raises `NoAppException` [`src/flask/cli.py:148-161`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L148-L161).</details>

## Data and state

### Where state lives, and for how long

*core · 6 min*

**In short:** Flask state has four lifetimes: the app object (the process), the app context and `g` (one context, usually one request), the request context (one request), and the session (across requests, in a cookie).

Most Flask bugs are lifetime bugs: storing something in the wrong place and seeing it vanish, or leak between users. Here is where each kind of state lives.

**The app object, for the life of the process.** `config`, the registries, `url_map`, `blueprints`, the JSON provider, and `extensions`, a dict where extensions keep their engines and clients [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:371-388`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L371-L388). Every request and thread shares it, so treat it as read-only after setup.

**The app context and `g`, for one context.** `g` is a new `_AppCtxGlobals` object every time an app context is created [`src/flask/ctx.py:248`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L248). Each request pushes its own app context, so `g` is effectively per request. It is the right place for 'one database connection per request', which is what the tutorial's `get_db` does: open on first use, close in a `teardown_appcontext` function [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py:9-30`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py#L9-L30). `g` is a plain namespace with `get`, `pop`, `setdefault` and `in` [`src/flask/ctx.py:67-108`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L67-L108).

**The request context, for one request.** The `Request` object, the URL adapter, the session, the flashed messages read so far and the `after_this_request` callbacks [`src/flask/ctx.py:316-331`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L316-L331).

**The session, across requests.** Kept in a signed cookie on the client by default, so it survives restarts and works across workers, but it is visible to the user and limited in size (`MAX_COOKIE_SIZE` is 4093 bytes [`src/flask/app.py:207`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L207)). Flashed messages wait here under `_flashes` until `get_flashed_messages` pops them [`src/flask/helpers.py:376-379`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py#L376-L379).

A rule of thumb: settings in `app.config`, shared clients in `app.extensions`, per-request resources on `g`, per-user state in `session`, nothing in module globals.

> **Checkpoint:** Where should a per-request database connection live?
> - A module-level global
> - `app.config['DB']`
> - `g`, closed by a `teardown_appcontext` function
> - `session`
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>`g`, closed by a `teardown_appcontext` function. `g` is fresh for every app context and teardown runs when the context ends; the tutorial wires exactly that [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py:51-56`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py#L51-L56).</details>

### Configuration: `app.config` and its loaders

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** `app.config` is a dict subclass created from `default_config` plus the `FLASK_DEBUG` variable. Loaders copy only UPPERCASE keys, and a few app attributes read and write config keys directly.

When the app is constructed, `make_config` copies the 29 entries of `Flask.default_config` [`src/flask/app.py:178-210`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L178-L210), sets `DEBUG` from `FLASK_DEBUG`, and creates `config_class(root_path, defaults)` [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:482-496`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L482-L496). The root path is the app's package folder, or the instance folder with `instance_relative_config=True`; relative file names in the loaders are resolved against it.

The loaders, all methods on `Config` [`src/flask/config.py:50-100`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L50-L100):
- `from_object(obj)`: copy the uppercase attributes of a module, class or import string [`src/flask/config.py:250-254`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L250-L254).
- `from_pyfile(filename, silent=False)`: execute a Python file as a module, then `from_object` it [`src/flask/config.py:204-216`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L204-L216). The tutorial loads `instance/config.py` with `silent=True` so the file may be missing [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py:16-21`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py#L16-L21).
- `from_envvar(name)`: `from_pyfile` on the path stored in an environment variable.
- `from_file(filename, load=json.load)`: any loader returning a mapping, such as JSON or TOML.
- `from_mapping(...)`: a dict or keyword arguments.
- `from_prefixed_env(prefix="FLASK")`: every `FLASK_*` variable, JSON-decoded when possible (`FLASK_PORT=8000` becomes the int 8000), with `__` building nested dicts [`src/flask/config.py:161-183`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L161-L183).

All but the last skip lowercase keys [`src/flask/config.py:318-320`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L318-L320), so a config file can use lowercase helper variables.

Some keys are also attributes. `ConfigAttribute` is a descriptor that forwards `app.testing` to `config['TESTING']`, `app.secret_key` to `SECRET_KEY`, and `app.permanent_session_lifetime` to `PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME`, converting an int of seconds to a `timedelta` [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:208-228`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L208-L228). `app.debug` is a real property that also updates Jinja's auto-reload [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:562-567`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L562-L567). `get_namespace('MAIL_')` returns the `MAIL_*` keys with the prefix removed and lowercased [`src/flask/config.py:323-364`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L323-L364).

> **Checkpoint:** `app.config.from_mapping(secret_key='abc')` runs during setup. Is the session secret key set?
> - Yes
> - No; `from_mapping` only copies uppercase keys
> - Yes, after a restart
> - It raises KeyError
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>No; `from_mapping` only copies uppercase keys. Lowercase keys are skipped [`src/flask/config.py:318-320`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L318-L320); use `SECRET_KEY='abc'`.</details>

### Inside the session cookie: tagged JSON

*deep · 5 min*

**In short:** The session cookie is tagged JSON, compactly encoded, timestamped and HMAC-signed. Tags let tuples, bytes, datetimes, UUIDs and Markup survive the trip through JSON.

JSON has no tuples, bytes or dates. Serializing `session['when'] = datetime.now()` with plain JSON would fail, and a tuple would come back as a list. `TaggedJSONSerializer` fixes this with tags [`src/flask/json/tag.py:219-247`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L219-L247).

`tag(value)` applies the first matching tag in this order: `TagDict`, `PassDict`, `TagTuple`, `PassList`, `TagBytes`, `TagMarkup`, `TagUUID`, `TagDateTime` [`src/flask/json/tag.py:289-295`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L289-L295). A tagged value becomes a one-key dict whose key starts with a space, so it is unlikely to clash with your own keys: `(1, 2)` becomes `{" t": [1, 2]}`, `b"x"` becomes `{" b": "eA=="}`, a datetime becomes `{" d": "Wed, 01 Jan 2025 00:00:00 GMT"}`. Dicts and lists pass through with their items tagged recursively. A real one-key dict like `{" t": 1}` is protected by `TagDict`, which wraps it in a `" di"` tag and renames the key to `" t__"` [`src/flask/json/tag.py:93-116`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L93-L116).

`loads` reverses this: decode the JSON, then `_untag_scan` rebuilds values bottom-up, turning every one-key dict with a registered tag back into the original type [`src/flask/json/tag.py:297-319`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L297-L319). `dumps` uses compact separators to save cookie bytes [`src/flask/json/tag.py:321-323`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L321-L323).

The session interface hands this serializer to ItsDangerous [`src/flask/sessions.py:287`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L287) [`src/flask/sessions.py:314`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L314), which adds the timestamp and signature and checks both before the JSON is parsed on the way back in.

Two consequences. You can teach the session a new type by registering a tag, as the module docstring shows [`src/flask/json/tag.py:16-41`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L16-L41). And datetimes go through the HTTP date format [`src/flask/json/tag.py:205-216`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L205-L216), so they keep whole seconds only and come back in UTC; store ISO strings yourself if you need more.

### JSON: the `app.json` provider

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** `app.json` is an object, not a module: `DefaultJSONProvider` wraps the standard library with sorted keys, ASCII escaping and extra types, and you replace it by subclassing.

Every JSON operation in Flask goes through the app's provider, created in `App.__init__` as `self.json = self.json_provider_class(self)` [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:329`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L329). Who calls it:
- dict or list return values from views [`src/flask/app.py:1230-1231`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1230-L1231);
- `jsonify(...)` [`src/flask/json/__init__.py:138-170`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/__init__.py#L138-L170);
- `request.get_json()`, because each request gets `json_module = app.json` [`src/flask/ctx.py:317-319`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L317-L319);
- the test client's `response.get_json()` [`src/flask/testing.py:240`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/testing.py#L240);
- Jinja's `|tojson` filter, through the `json.dumps_function` policy [`src/flask/app.py:422`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L422);
- `flask.json.dumps` and `loads` when an app context is active, falling back to the standard library otherwise [`src/flask/json/__init__.py:40-44`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/__init__.py#L40-L44).

`DefaultJSONProvider` sets three defaults on `json.dumps`: `default=_default`, `ensure_ascii=True`, `sort_keys=True` [`src/flask/json/provider.py:166-179`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/provider.py#L166-L179). `_default` turns dates into HTTP date strings, `Decimal` and `UUID` into strings, dataclasses into dicts and anything with `__html__` into its HTML [`src/flask/json/provider.py:108-121`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/provider.py#L108-L121). `response()` indents by 2 in debug mode when `compact` is `None`, otherwise uses compact separators, and always ends with a newline [`src/flask/json/provider.py:189-215`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/provider.py#L189-L215).

To customize, subclass and change attributes or methods, then set `json_provider_class` on a `Flask` subclass, or assign `app.json = MyProvider(app)` during setup [`src/flask/json/provider.py:19-36`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/provider.py#L19-L36). The provider keeps only a weak proxy to the app to avoid a reference cycle [`src/flask/json/provider.py:38-39`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/provider.py#L38-L39). This design replaced config keys such as `JSON_SORT_KEYS`, removed in 2.3 [`CHANGES.rst:153-154`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L153-L154).

## File by file

### The five engine files, in reading order

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** Five files hold the engine: `globals.py`, `ctx.py`, `sansio/scaffold.py`, `sansio/app.py` and `app.py`. Read them smallest first; each makes the next easier.

1. `globals.py` (51 lines). Two ContextVars and six proxies. Ten minutes and you know what `request` is.
2. `ctx.py` (449 lines). `AppContext`, `RequestContext` and `g`. Focus on `push` and `pop` [`src/flask/ctx.py:367-431`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L367-L431); skip the docstrings.
3. `sansio/scaffold.py` (792 lines). The registries in `__init__` and the decorators. Most decorator bodies are one or two lines, so this goes fast. Skip `_find_package_path` unless you work on instance paths.
4. `sansio/app.py` (964 lines). Class attributes first, because they are the customization points, then `__init__`, `add_url_rule` and `_find_error_handler`.
5. `app.py` (1,536 lines). Read `wsgi_app`, `full_dispatch_request`, `dispatch_request`, `finalize_request`, `make_response`, `preprocess_request` and `process_response` together; they are one pipeline. Then the error trio: `handle_user_exception`, `handle_http_exception`, `handle_exception`.

The line counts overstate the logic. About 700 of `app.py`'s lines are docstrings and roughly 470 are code; across `src/flask`, docstrings are about a third of all lines. A fast way in is to read only the `def` lines of a file first.

Two things trip readers. Methods with the same name exist in both halves: `Scaffold.add_url_rule` is a documented stub that raises [`src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py:367-433`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py#L367-L433), while `App.add_url_rule` is the real one [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:604-661`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L604-L661). And some methods are hooks for subclasses even though Flask never changes them, such as `should_ignore_error`, which always returns `False` [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:883-891`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L883-L891) but is consulted on every request with an error [`src/flask/app.py:1524-1525`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1524-L1525).

The cards below list the symbols worth opening in each file.

### Feature modules and where they plug in

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** The feature modules are small and independent: each plugs into the pipeline at one or two named points, so you can read any of them on its own.

Each feature attaches to the core through a class attribute or a single call site.

- `wrappers.py` plugs in through `request_class` and `response_class`. `Request` adds routing results and config-backed size limits; `Response` sets `text/html` and reads `MAX_COOKIE_SIZE` from config [`src/flask/wrappers.py:246-257`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/wrappers.py#L246-L257).
- `sessions.py` plugs in through `session_interface`, called at context push and in `process_response`.
- `templating.py` plugs in through `jinja_environment` and `create_global_jinja_loader`; views call `render_template`.
- `json/` plugs in through `json_provider_class`; `make_response` and `jsonify` call it.
- `helpers.py` is the public toolbox. Most functions delegate to `current_app` so an app subclass can override them: `url_for` calls `app.url_for`, `redirect` calls `app.redirect`, `abort` calls `app.aborter` [`src/flask/helpers.py:232-286`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py#L232-L286).
- `views.py` builds view functions from classes and depends only on `current_app`, `request` and the type aliases [`src/flask/views.py:1-13`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/views.py#L1-L13).
- `blueprints.py` and `sansio/blueprints.py` sit on top of everything else and call the app's own registration methods.

A useful habit: when you wonder where Flask uses a feature, search `app.py` for the attribute name (`session_interface`, `json`, `jinja_env`). There are only a handful of call sites, because these parts were designed to be replaceable.

### Developer tooling: CLI, test client, logging, debug helpers

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** `cli.py`, `testing.py`, `logging.py` and `debughelpers.py` serve developers rather than requests. They use the core, but the core only imports them lazily or to create `app.cli`.

These files sit at the edge: `app.py` imports `debughelpers` and `testing` lazily, inside the functions that need them [`src/flask/app.py:502`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L502) [`src/flask/app.py:720-722`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L720-L722), and imports the CLI module only to create `app.cli`.

- `cli.py` (1,127 lines) is the biggest after `app.py`. Read `ScriptInfo.load_app`, `find_best_app`, `FlaskGroup.get_command` and `run_command`. The SSL option types (`CertParamType`, `_validate_key`) only matter for `flask run --cert`.
- `testing.py` (298 lines). `FlaskClient` is where `with client:` preserves contexts and `session_transaction()` edits the session through a temporary request context [`src/flask/testing.py:135-183`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/testing.py#L135-L183). `FlaskCliRunner` runs `app.cli` commands in tests.
- `logging.py` (79 lines). `app.logger` is `logging.getLogger(app.name)`; Flask adds its own handler only when nothing would handle the logger's level, so your logging config wins [`src/flask/logging.py:58-79`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/logging.py#L58-L79). The default handler writes to `wsgi.errors` during a request and to stderr otherwise [`src/flask/logging.py:15-28`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/logging.py#L15-L28).
- `debughelpers.py` (178 lines). Active only in debug mode: clearer errors for forms posted without `enctype="multipart/form-data"`, for POSTs redirected to a trailing-slash URL [`src/flask/app.py:494-504`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L494-L504), and the template-loading report.

For Flask's own suite, `tests/conftest.py` is the companion file: fixtures, environment resets and the context leak detector.

## How it was built

### Fifteen years of Flask: the changes that shaped it

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Flask grew from a 2010 single-module wrapper into a typed, split package. The big reshapes were the Click CLI (2014), the src layout and Scaffold (2019-2020), async and nested blueprints (2021), contextvars and JSON providers (2022), and the sans-IO split (2023).

Git history starts with Armin Ronacher's 'Initial checkin of stuff that exists so far' on 2010-04-06 (`33850c0e`); documentation was started the same day (`4ec7d2a0`) and has been written alongside the code ever since. `CHANGES.rst` is the most reliable narrative, with every version's changes and issue numbers.

The changes that shaped today's code:
- **2014, Click.** `3bdb90f0` replaced the old runner with a Click-based `cli.py`; it shipped in 0.11 (2016).
- **2019, src layout.** `ca278a86` moved the package into `src/flask/`.
- **2020, Scaffold.** `b146a13f` pulled the API shared by `Flask` and `Blueprint` into one base class, which is why both have identical decorators today.
- **2021, Flask 2.0.** `async def` support via asgiref (`6979265f`) and nested blueprints (`f92e820b`), whose dotted endpoint names drive scoped hooks.
- **2022, Flask 2.2.** Contexts moved from Werkzeug's `LocalStack` to `ContextVar` (`d597db67`), `app.json` providers arrived (`69f9845e`), and `before_first_request` was deprecated (`96c97dec`).
- **2023, Flask 2.3 and 3.0.** 2.3 removed a long list of deprecated APIs [`CHANGES.rst:135-160`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L135-L160) and 2.3.3 moved packaging to flit (`f38f3a74`); 3.0 split the code into `sansio/` and I/O halves for Quart (`0ec7f713`) [`CHANGES.rst:92-101`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L92-L101).
- **2024-2025, Flask 3.1.** Key rotation (`e13373f8`), resource limits and `TRUSTED_HOSTS` [`CHANGES.rst:25-54`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L25-L54), then a security fix for the signing-key order (`fb541598`) and the switch to uv (`0109e496`).

Activity has slowed: 172 commits in 2024 and 51 in 2025 up to June, against 260 to 560 a year before that. The project is mature; most current work is maintenance, typing and removals, and the unreleased 3.2.0 so far only drops Python 3.9 and removes `__version__` [`CHANGES.rst:1-7`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L1-L7).

### Build order: how you would write Flask again

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** If you rebuilt Flask you would start with leaf modules (config, signals, context storage), then the registry, the sans-IO app and the WSGI pipeline, and finish with sessions, templates, blueprints, the CLI and the public package.

The import graph gives the order: modules that everything depends on come first, modules nothing depends on come last. Read the milestones below as a build plan; each ends with something to try in a shell.

The shape of the plan:
1. **Foundations** that import nothing from Flask: `config.py`, `signals.py`, `typing.py`. `Config` is a dict with a root path [`src/flask/config.py:94-100`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/config.py#L94-L100).
2. **Context storage**: `globals.py`, then `ctx.py`. You can push and pop contexts before any routing exists.
3. **The registry**: `Scaffold` and `setupmethod`. Decorators now store functions, but nothing calls them yet.
4. **The sans-IO app**: config creation, `add_url_rule`, error-handler lookup.
5. **Request and Response** subclasses.
6. **The pipeline**: `Flask.wsgi_app` and its helpers. A request can now reach a view.
7. **Sessions, templates, JSON**: features that plug into named points.
8. **Blueprints**: a recorder in front of the app's registration methods.
9. **CLI, test client, class-based views, debug helpers**: developer tools at the edge.
10. **`__init__.py`**: re-export the public API last.

Two dependencies are less obvious. `ctx.py` comes before the app, yet `AppContext.__init__` calls `app.create_url_adapter` and `app.app_ctx_globals_class` [`src/flask/ctx.py:245-249`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L245-L249), so the context classes depend on the app's interface, not its implementation. And `templating.py` is needed by `Scaffold`, because the default context processor lives there [`src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py:19`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py#L19).

The scanner's own import graph treats the standard library's `typing` and `json` as Flask modules in a few places, so prefer this hand-checked order over raw 'used by' counts.

## Why it's like this

### The choices behind Flask's shape

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** Flask's shape follows a few explicit choices: an explicit app object, context-local globals, Werkzeug and Jinja as foundations, signed-cookie sessions, async on threads, and a sans-IO core. Each has a cost worth knowing.

Each decision record below says what was chosen, why, what it costs, and whether the reason is documented (a commit, doc or comment) or inferred from the code. Three themes connect them.

**A small core with replaceable parts.** Flask picks defaults but exposes each one as a class attribute or object you can swap: `session_interface`, `json_provider_class`, `request_class`, `jinja_environment`, `url_map_class`. The design notes put it bluntly: Flask will never have a database layer, and everything else is up for extensions [`docs/design.rst:206-213`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/docs/design.rst#L206-L213).

**Convenience over purity.** Context-local proxies keep views short at the cost of hidden state; the design notes admit thread locals 'cause troubles' [`docs/design.rst:172-184`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/docs/design.rst#L172-L184). The explicit app object is the counterweight: you always know which app you configure [`docs/design.rst:36-45`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/docs/design.rst#L36-L45).

**Compatibility over novelty.** Async views run through asgiref on the worker thread so existing WSGI extensions keep working [`docs/design.rst:187-203`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/docs/design.rst#L187-L203). APIs are usually deprecated with warnings for a release before they are removed, which is why `CHANGES.rst` has long 'removed' lists [`CHANGES.rst:135-160`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L135-L160).

When you propose a change, check it against these themes. A change that adds a dependency, hard-codes a choice an extension might want to override, or breaks the context model will probably meet resistance; a change that makes a default replaceable usually fits.

### Why context locals, and why ContextVar

*deep · 5 min*

**In short:** Flask chose global-looking proxies so views stay short. In 2022 the implementation moved from Werkzeug's `LocalStack` to plain `ContextVar`s, which also made contexts behave correctly under asyncio.

The alternative design, passing `request` into every view, is what many frameworks do. Flask instead lets any code read `request`, `session`, `g` and `current_app`, accepting the downsides because it optimizes for quick, traditional web apps [`docs/design.rst:172-184`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/docs/design.rst#L172-L184). The cost is that such code silently depends on a pushed context, which is why Flask has `has_request_context()`, the 'Working outside of ...' messages, `test_request_context()` and `app_context()`.

Before Flask 2.2 the contexts lived on Werkzeug `LocalStack` objects, `_app_ctx_stack` and `_request_ctx_stack`: stacks stored per thread or greenlet. Commit `d597db67` ('contexts no longer use LocalStack', 2022-07-04) replaced them with two `ContextVar`s, and each context now keeps its own list of tokens instead of a shared stack [`src/flask/ctx.py:249`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L249) [`src/flask/ctx.py:333-335`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L333-L335). The 2.3 release removed the deprecated stacks' `push` and `pop` [`CHANGES.rst:145-147`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/CHANGES.rst#L145-L147).

Why it matters:
- A `ContextVar` is separate per thread and per asyncio task, so contexts behave correctly under asgiref and in Quart.
- Tokens make nesting exact: `reset(token)` restores precisely the previous value, and a mismatched pop is detected [`src/flask/ctx.py:264-270`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L264-L270).
- There is no custom stack code left to maintain.

One subtlety remains. In standard CPython a new thread starts with an empty context, so a thread started from a view must push its own context or receive the data it needs. `copy_current_request_context` covers the greenlet case [`src/flask/ctx.py:155-193`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L155-L193).

## Handle with care

### What to handle with care

*core · 6 min*

**In short:** The risks that bite real apps are readable session cookies, a placeholder secret key, debug mode in production, unsafe file paths, and session changes that silently do not save. The framework's own code has only low-severity rough edges.

The list below is ordered by severity, each with the exact place in the code. The headline items are about using Flask safely; the framework itself is mature and heavily tested.

**Security of the defaults.**
- The session cookie is signed, not encrypted [`src/flask/sessions.py:298-301`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L298-L301), so users can read it. Keep secrets and personal data out of `session`.
- Everything rests on `SECRET_KEY`. Flask refuses to write sessions without one, but it cannot tell a strong key from the tutorial's placeholder `dev` [`examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py:9-14`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py#L9-L14).
- Debug mode enables an in-browser debugger that can run code; it must never be on in production [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:549-560`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L549-L560).
- `send_file` trusts its path; serve user-chosen files with `send_from_directory` [`src/flask/helpers.py:418-421`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py#L418-L421).

**Silent behaviour.**
- Mutating a list or dict inside the session does not mark it modified [`src/flask/sessions.py:61-66`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L61-L66).
- Changing config or the Jinja environment after the first request is not detected; only setup-method calls are [`docs/lifecycle.rst:50-61`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/docs/lifecycle.rst#L50-L61).

**Rough edges in the code.**
- `Flask.open_resource` defaults to the locale's encoding while its blueprint twin uses UTF-8.
- The devcontainer script installs from a deleted `requirements/` folder.
- Leftovers from removed features (`BeforeFirstRequestCallable`, a Python 2 docstring example).

None of the code-level items are security problems. They make good first contributions, and three of them are exercises in the last chapter.

> **Checkpoint:** A teammate wants to store the user's email address in `session` to save a database query. What is the main concern?
> - Sessions cannot store strings
> - The default session cookie can be read by the client; it is signed, not encrypted
> - Email addresses are too long for cookies
> - It turns off the Vary: Cookie header
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The default session cookie can be read by the client; it is signed, not encrypted. The default interface only signs the data with ItsDangerous [`src/flask/sessions.py:317-335`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L317-L335); signing prevents changes, not reading.</details>

### Six behaviours that surprise people

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Hook order, teardown timing, exception propagation in tests, the lifetime of `g`, an ignored `app.run()`, and after-request functions re-running on errors. None are bugs; each has cost someone an afternoon.

1. **After-hooks run in reverse.** `after_request` and `teardown_request` functions run in reverse registration order, innermost blueprint first [`src/flask/app.py:1316-1319`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1316-L1319); `test_before_after_request_order` pins it down [`tests/test_basic.py:829-864`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/tests/test_basic.py#L829-L864).
2. **Teardown cannot change the response.** It runs in `wsgi_app`'s `finally`, after the response object is built, and it only receives the exception [`src/flask/app.py:1519-1527`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L1519-L1527). For a streamed body, the context is already gone when the server reads the generator, which is why `stream_with_context` exists.
3. **Tests see exceptions, production sees 500s.** `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` defaults to `None`, meaning 'on when testing or debugging' [`src/flask/app.py:841-852`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L841-L852). A test that expects a 500 page must set `app.testing = False` or the key to `False`.
4. **`g` is not a cache.** It is recreated with each app context, so every request starts with an empty `g` [`src/flask/ctx.py:248`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py#L248).
5. **`app.run()` does nothing under `flask run`.** The CLI sets `FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI` and `run` returns early with a warning [`src/flask/app.py:609-621`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L609-L621).
6. **After-request functions can run twice.** If one raises outside testing and debug mode, `handle_exception` finalizes a 500 response, and `process_response` runs the after-request functions again, including those that already succeeded [`src/flask/app.py:854-862`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L854-L862). This is inferred from the code; keep them idempotent.

A seventh, for contributors: a blueprint's setup methods fail after its first registration and an app's after its first request, in tests too. Build a fresh app per test, as `tests/conftest.py` does [`tests/conftest.py:44-51`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/tests/conftest.py#L44-L51).

## Your first changes

### Your first changes to Flask

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Eight real changes, from deleting a dead type alias to adding async URL value preprocessors. Each names the files to touch and how you know it worked.

The exercises below use this repository, not a toy app. The easy ones are small real improvements found while writing this guide, and each teaches part of the tooling: tests, type checking, tox.

Before you start any of them:
1. Run `uv sync` and `uv run pytest` to see a green baseline.
2. Read the test file next to the code you will change. Flask's tests are short functions that build an app inline, so the pattern is easy to copy; `test_session` is typical [`tests/test_basic.py:234-254`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/tests/test_basic.py#L234-L254).
3. Remember that warnings are errors [`pyproject.toml:107-111`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/pyproject.toml#L107-L111), and that `uv run tox run -e typing` must pass for any change to a signature.

A suggested path by goal:
- **Learn the pipeline:** 'Pin down after_request behaviour when one raises', then 'Write a server-side session interface'.
- **Learn the CLI:** 'Add a `flask config` command'.
- **Learn typing and the sans-IO split:** 'Support async URL value preprocessors'. It forces you to decide which half of the code owns the change.
- **Learn the provider pattern:** 'A JSON provider with ISO dates'.

When an exercise changes behaviour, write the test first and watch it fail. The suite's `leak_detector` fixture will also tell you if your change leaves a context pushed [`tests/conftest.py:84-95`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/tests/conftest.py#L84-L95).

## Reference

### Stack

| Technology | Role | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Werkzeug | Parses the WSGI environ into `Request`, builds `Response`, provides URL routing (`Map`, `Rule`, `MapAdapter`), HTTP exceptions, `LocalProxy`, the test client and the development server. | [`src/flask/wrappers.py:7-8`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/wrappers.py#L7-L8) [`src/flask/sansio/app.py:14-15`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py#L14-L15) |
| Jinja2 | Renders HTML templates. Flask subclasses its `Environment`, plugs in a loader that searches the app and every blueprint, and turns autoescaping on for .html/.xml/.svg. | [`src/flask/templating.py:39-49`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/templating.py#L39-L49) |
| MarkupSafe | Provides `Markup`, the 'already safe HTML' string type. The session serializer round-trips it with its own tag. | [`src/flask/json/tag.py:173-188`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/json/tag.py#L173-L188) |
| ItsDangerous | Signs the session cookie with `SECRET_KEY` so the client cannot change it, and checks its age on the way back in. | [`src/flask/sessions.py:317-335`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py#L317-L335) |
| Click | Implements the `flask` command: option parsing, command groups, `flask run`, `flask shell`, `flask routes` and every `@app.cli.command()`. | [`src/flask/cli.py:531`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L531) |
| Blinker | Provides the ten built-in signals (`request_started`, `template_rendered`, ...) that extensions and tests subscribe to. | [`src/flask/signals.py:1-17`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/signals.py#L1-L17) |
| contextvars + LocalProxy | Store 'the current app' and 'the current request' per thread or per async task, and expose them as the global-looking objects `current_app`, `g`, `request` and `session`. | [`src/flask/globals.py:24-51`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/globals.py#L24-L51) |
| asgiref (optional) | Runs `async def` views and hooks by converting them to blocking calls with `async_to_sync`. | [`src/flask/app.py:994-1001`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py#L994-L1001) |
| python-dotenv (optional) | Loads `.flaskenv` and `.env` files into `os.environ` when the CLI starts. | [`src/flask/cli.py:745-763`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/cli.py#L745-L763) |
| pytest, tox, uv | pytest runs `tests/`; tox defines the Python-version, minimum-dependency, style, typing and docs environments; uv installs from `uv.lock` and drives tox in CI. | [`pyproject.toml:171-193`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/pyproject.toml#L171-L193) |
| mypy, pyright, ruff | mypy (strict) and pyright type-check `src/` and `tests/type_check`; ruff lints and formats through pre-commit. | [`pyproject.toml:127-146`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/pyproject.toml#L127-L146) |
| flit_core | Builds the wheel and sdist from `pyproject.toml`; `flask = "flask.cli:main"` becomes the `flask` executable. | [`pyproject.toml:82-90`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/pyproject.toml#L82-L90) |

### Files

- [`src/flask/__init__.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/__init__.py): Defines what `import flask` gives you.
- [`src/flask/__main__.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/__main__.py): Makes `python -m flask` work.
- [`src/flask/app.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/app.py): The `Flask` class: the WSGI entry point and the request pipeline.
- [`src/flask/sansio/app.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/app.py): The `App` base class: config, URL map, registries and error-handler lookup, with no I/O.
- [`src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py): `Scaffold`, the shared base of app and blueprint: decorators and the hook registries.
- [`src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py): `Blueprint` and `BlueprintSetupState`: deferred registration.
- [`src/flask/sansio/README.md`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sansio/README.md): The rule for the sansio folder.
- [`src/flask/blueprints.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/blueprints.py): The I/O half of `Blueprint`: CLI group, static files, resources.
- [`src/flask/ctx.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/ctx.py): `AppContext`, `RequestContext` and `g`.
- [`src/flask/globals.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/globals.py): The two ContextVars and the proxies built on them.
- [`src/flask/wrappers.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/wrappers.py): Flask's `Request` and `Response` subclasses of Werkzeug's.
- [`src/flask/helpers.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/helpers.py): Public helper functions: `url_for`, `redirect`, `abort`, `flash`, `send_file`, `stream_with_context`.
- [`src/flask/sessions.py`](https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/85c5d93cbd049c4bd0679c36fd1ddcae8c37b642/src/flask/sessions.py): Session interface and the default signed-cookie session.
